standard.title: Technical Guidelines for Consumer Products Dealing Establishments Compliance

notes.module_kind_justification: GU83 is the strongest compliance module of this group. It states a fixed requirement set (14 annexes), assigns each requirement a risk class in the document itself, defines the required action per risk class (section 8), and defines a grading formula from A to F driven by counts of violations by class (section 9). A report can therefore legitimately say 'grade C, 2 Critical and 4 Major violations' and, where zero violations, that the establishment complies. This is a verdict the source document authorises.
notes.verdict_caution: The verdict GU83 authorises is a GRADE, not a binary. There is no 'COMPLIANT' band: grade A still tolerates 1 to 2 Minor violations. A report must emit the grade letter plus the violation counts, never a bare COMPLIANT/NON-COMPLIANT, because collapsing A-F to a binary invents a threshold DM did not set.
notes.version_conflict: The cover page and every page footer say Version # V 4.1, Issue Date 9th June 2025, Superseded Issue Date 28th April 2024. The Document History Log on page 2 tops out at version '3', dated 9th June 2025. The document therefore disagrees with itself about its own version number: the history log has no row for 4.0 or 4.1. The cover/footer value (4.1) is used here because it is the value stamped on all 35 pages, but this must be re-verified before the module is sold. The URL says V4.1 and happens to agree with the cover - that agreement is coincidence and was not relied on.
notes.annex_cross_reference_error: Section 10 of the body cites the wrong annex numbers, systematically off by one from Part E for everything after Annex 1. Section 10-3(I) sends toys to 'Annex 5', but Annex 5 is Noise control and toys are Annex 6. 10-3(II) sends food contact materials to Annex 6 (actually 7), 10-3(III) cosmetics to Annex 7 (actually 8), 10-3(IV) low voltage to Annex 8 (actually 9), 10-3(V) health supplements to Annex 9 (actually 10), 10-3(VI) detergents to Annex 10 (actually 11), 10-3(VII) biocides to Annex 11 (actually 12), 10-3(VIII) tobacco to Annex 12 (actually 13). 10-4 sends indoor air to 'Annex 2', but Annex 2 is Public Safety and indoor air is Annex 3. 10-2 cites 'Annex 1, Annex 13' for public and operational safety, where the actual public-safety annex is Annex 2. The extraction below binds each template to the ANNEX AS PRINTED IN PART E, whose own headings are unambiguous, and ignores section 10's pointers. Do not build applicability routing from section 10.
notes.applicability_gap: The document never states which annexes apply to which business activity. Part E is titled 'Business activity Annexes' and section 8 notes 'Each requirement violation assessed to its risk based on business activity type', but no activity-to-annex mapping is printed anywhere. A perfume shop is plainly not assessed against the swimming-pool or toys items, yet nothing in GU83 says so. applies_to on each template below is derived from the annex's own heading, NOT from a stated scope rule. Any activity-based filtering the app applies is the app's own judgement and must be labelled as such - this is the single largest content gap in GU83 and it must be resolved with DM before the module ships, because serving the wrong annex set changes the grade.
notes.severity_enum: The document uses a FOUR-level failure scale: Minor, Major, Critical, Catastrophic. The extraction schema's enum (critical|major|minor|unknown) has no slot for Catastrophic, and collapsing it into 'critical' would be a real error rather than a cosmetic one: under the section 9 formula ONE Catastrophic is grade F on its own, whereas it takes FIVE Criticals to reach F. The enum must be extended. failure_severity carries the extended value; source_risk_label carries the document's verbatim label in every case.
notes.duplicates: Annex 5 prints 'Noise source entertainment premise operating out from residential area.' twice and Annex 7 prints 'Not to deal in misleading or improper details of food contact materials.' twice. Both are flagged with duplicate_of. Scoring the duplicates independently double-counts one real failure and can move the grade down a band.
notes.out_of_scale_severity: Two Annex 5 items are labelled 'Low', which is not one of the four risk-assessment outcomes. They are set to failure_severity 'unknown' and cannot enter the grading formula.
notes.numbering: The annexes print requirements as unnumbered table rows. Item numbers below (A<annex>.<row>) are positional and assigned by this extraction. Item TEXT is verbatim including the document's own typographical errors ('inscects', 'Prsence', 'AvaiIability', 'driniking', 'belowacceptable', 'nad', 'disseased'), which are preserved deliberately so the attested wording matches the source.
notes.response_type: All items are recorded as yes_no_na. The document does not print a response format at all - it prints a requirement and a risk class, and an inspector records a violation or not. yes_no_na is the honest reading (many items are inapplicable to a given activity - see applicability_gap), but it is this extraction's inference, not the document's instruction.

matrix.note: Rows are 'Probability of repetition', columns are 'Severity of the potential risk'. The cell value is the RISK ASSESSMENT class used by section 9 grading.

grading.source_quote: Establishment's violations to the environmental health requirements shall affect overall grade as per below formulas settled as per management decisions: Where highest level of compliance score A grade, in descending order to grade F.
grading.evaluation_order: F first, then D, C, B, A - the first grade whose condition is satisfied wins. The document prints the table F-to-A and the bands are not mutually exclusive if read in the other direction.
unresolved: There is no grade E. The document says grades run A to F but prints only A, B, C, D and F.

Grades A and B overlap and are not separable as printed: A is '0 Critical and/or 0 Major and/or 1 TO 2 Minor' and B is '0 Critical and/or 0 Major and/or 1 TO 3 Minor'. An establishment with 0 Critical, 0 Major and 2 Minor satisfies BOTH. Neither band mentions Catastrophic. A zero-violation establishment matches no band at all.
The combinator is printed as '&/or' throughout, which is not a decidable operator. Whether the bands are conjunctive or disjunctive changes the grade for most real inspections.

Because of the above, the grading formula MUST NOT be implemented as an automatic scorer without written clarification from DM. Emit the violation counts by class and, at most, a provisional grade clearly marked as derived. A wrong grade letter on a report is exactly the misrepresentation section 7.12 warns about.

checklist_templates.label: Annex 14: Tobacco products and premise control requirements.

items.text: Prohibit sale and Displaying tobacco and related products within health, sport and education entities, and worship buildings or its property.
Prohibit sale and Displaying tobacco and related product within 100 meters distance from worship buildings or its property.
Prohibit sale and Displaying tobacco and related products within 150 meters distance from nurseries, schools, institutes and universities outer entrances.
Providing valid permit for displaying and selling tobacco and related products.
Place clear permit copy in a prominent place inside premise.
Prohibit sale and Displaying tobacco and related products via internet or any electronic means .
Commitment to not advertise or promote tobacco and its products, and/or displaying free samples.
Prohibit sale and Displaying tobacco and related products near foodstuff or sport tools and cloth or sanitary and children products is prohibited.
Prohibit sale and Displaying tobacco and related products near cashiers or shall be as far as possible.
Prohibit sale and Displaying tobacco and related products during events or in festival activities without permit from concerned authority.
Prohibit sale and Displaying tobacco and related products for person under 18 years old.
Prohibit the presence and or of sale for persons under 18 years in tobacco and related products specialized premises .
Availability of proper security system for in and out monitoring and assure of no entrance to person under 18 years in tobacco and related products specialized premises .
Not exceeding allowed working hours ( From 10 AM To 12 AM ) for seeling and serve tobacco and related products, without permit from concerned authority.

obligations.cadence_note: Routine inspection frequency is set by the establishment's own grade, but the document does not print the grade-to-frequency mapping. No cadence can be encoded from GU83 alone.
obligations.source_quote: Routine: scheduled visit based on premise grade.

obligations.trigger_event: remarks detected upon previous findings risk
obligations.source_quote: Follow-Up: scheduled visit according to remarks detected upon previous findings risk.
Complaint: Enforced unexpected visit scheduled upon incidences received.

obligations.trigger_event: management decision, memo or case investigation
obligations.source_quote: Management Order: Enforced expected visit scheduled upon management decisions, memos or during case investigation.

obligations.trigger_event: quality issues or field status changes
obligations.source_quote: Random: Non-Forced unexpected inspection according to quality issues, or could be determined on the status and changes in the field.

obligations.applies_to: Consumer products, non-drinking water and indoor air
obligations.source_quote: Sampling: Enforced expected visit scheduled specifically for consumer products and/or non-drinking water and/or indoor air sample site measurement and collection for the purpose of testing and determine environmental health conditions, however, it may processed in conjunction with previous types of visits.

obligations.cadence_note: Self-inspection is named as a monitoring mode but no frequency is given.
obligations.source_quote: Notification and case investigation with establishment remotely via self-inspection or during investigation visit.

obligations.cadence_note: 'Periodical' is stated but the period is not. This is an Annex 2 checklist item (Minor) as well as an obligation.
obligations.source_quote: Submission of periodical test reports on Dubai Municipality - health and safety compliance portal.

obligations.cadence_note: A grace period exists for disputing a report but its length is declared in the issued report, not in the guideline. Cannot be encoded from GU83.
obligations.source_quote: Disputing and review process has guaranteed for Dubai Municipality customer within declared grace period declared in report issued
